chunks: From him, from his father, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from al-Hasan ibn Matil, from Sahl ibn Ziyad al-Adami, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah, from Salih ibn Uqbah, from Abu Shibl, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I visit the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him).' He said: 'Visit the grave of al-Tayyib (the Pure One) and complete the prayer near it.' I said: 'Complete the prayer?' He said: 'Complete it.' I said: 'Some of our companions consider it permissible to shorten it.' He said: 'Only the weaklings do that.'

key_terms.إِتْمَامُ الصَّلَاةِ: Completing the prayer (praying four rak'ahs instead of two)
key_terms.التَّقْصِيرَ: Shortening the prayer (praying two rak'ahs instead of four)
key_terms.الضُّعَفَةُ: The weaklings (those with weak faith or practice)
key_terms.قَبْرَ الطَّيِّبِ: The grave of al-Tayyib (a title for Imam al-Husayn)

ai.seo_question: Should one shorten or complete the prayer when visiting the grave of Imam al-Husayn?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ruling on praying *tamam* (full four-rak'ah prayer) rather than *qasr* (shortened) when visiting the shrine of Imam al-Husayn (AS) in Kufa, distinguishing it from the general rule for travelers. He attributes the practice of shortening the prayer to the 'weak' (*al-du'afa*) among the companions, indicating that while permissible, it reflects a lesser degree of spiritual commitment or adherence to the specific recommendation of the shrine's sanctity. This highlights the unique status of the Haram of Kufa as a place where the full prayer is preferred to honor the presence of the Imam.
